free_text: The decision was driven by the conflict between low-grade histology (Gleason 3+3) and severe symptomatic burden (IPSS 35/35), compounded by the PI-RADS 4 lesion. The low Gleason score argues against immediate aggressive treatment, but the severe LUTS mandates intervention to improve quality of life. The combination of symptoms and imaging findings tipped the balance toward active treatment planning.
